name: RA_TERMS_B_
description: The RA_TERMS_B table stores standard payment term information. Oracle Receivables creates one row for each payment term that you define. Receivables uses this information to calculate when a payment is due and any discounts that are given for early payment. Receivables stores payment schedules in the AR_PAYMENT_SCHEDULES_ALL table. . The primary key for this table is TERM_ID.

columns.name: TERM_ID
columns.description: Payment term identifier

columns.name: MODULE_ID
columns.description: Seed Data Framework: indicates the module that owns the row. A module is an entry in Application Taxonomy such as a Logical Business Area. When the MODULE_ID column exists and the owner of the row is not specified, then the Seed Data Framework will not extract the row as seed data.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: NAME
columns.description: Payment term name.

columns.name: CREDIT_CHECK_FLAG
columns.description: Indicates whether the customer account is included in credit checking.

columns.name: DUE_CUTOFF_DAY
columns.description: Cutoff day with proxima terms when due date is extended one month

columns.name: PRINTING_LEAD_DAYS
columns.description: This is the number of days between the print date and the due date. If this column is null, the invoice is printed on the invoice date.  If this column is filled in, the invoice is printed this number of days before the due date.
